findings.title: Database Initialization Strategy Conflict
findings.problem: Design states 'Do NOT use db.create_all() alongside schema.sql' but models define defaults/onupdate that conflict with schema.sql MySQL defaults. TASSequence has default=0 in model AND DEFAULT 0 in schema. updated_at uses onupdate=datetime.utcnow in models AND ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in schema - these will conflict.
findings.fix: Choose ONE approach: (A) Schema-first - remove all default/onupdate from models that MySQL handles, document 'schema.sql is single source of truth for defaults', OR (B) ORM-first - remove DEFAULT/ON UPDATE from schema.sql, use db.create_all(). Recommended: Option A for this project.

findings.title: Missing CSRF Token Validation in Non-WTForm Routes
findings.location: Section 7 (TAS Management) - approve_tas and reject_tas routes
findings.problem: Templates include CSRF tokens but route implementations don't validate them. approve_tas and reject_tas don't use WTForms so automatic validation doesn't happen. Routes are vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
findings.fix: Add manual CSRF validation: 'from flask_wtf.csrf import validate_csrf; try: validate_csrf(request.form.get('csrf_token')); except ValidationError: abort(403)' at start of approve_tas and reject_tas routes. Document this pattern in Section 10.

findings.title: User.get_id() Type Safety Not Enforced
findings.problem: get_id() returns str(self.user_id) but no validation if user_id is None. user_loader does int(user_id) but no error handling for ValueError if session corrupted. This can cause crashes or security issues.
findings.fix: Update get_id(): 'if self.user_id is None: raise ValueError("User ID is None")'. Update user_loader: wrap int(user_id) in try/except (ValueError, TypeError): return None to force re-login on corrupted session.

findings.title: Race Condition in TAS Number Generation Despite Locking
findings.problem: When TASSequence row doesn't exist, two concurrent transactions can both see None and both try INSERT with last_sequence=1, causing PRIMARY KEY IntegrityError. Design doesn't specify recovery strategy for this race condition.
findings.fix: Wrap seq_record creation in try/except IntegrityError with max_retries=3. On IntegrityError: db.session.rollback() and retry (lock should succeed on existing row). Use db.session.flush() after add to detect conflict immediately. After 3 retries, raise RuntimeError.

findings.title: Unverified Assumption About datetime.utcnow() vs MySQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
findings.problem: Models use default=datetime.utcnow (application server time) and schema.sql uses DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (database server time in MySQL's configured timezone). These can differ if servers not synchronized or MySQL timezone != UTC. Design assumes 'timestamps in UTC' but doesn't enforce it.
findings.fix: Add to schema.sql header: 'SET time_zone = "+00:00";'. Add to config: ensure MySQL uses UTC timezone in my.cnf 'default-time-zone="+00:00"'. Clarify in Section 1: all timestamps use MySQL server-side defaults only (remove datetime.utcnow defaults from models) for consistency.

findings.title: Missing Transaction Isolation Level Specification
findings.problem: with_for_update() locking requires at least READ COMMITTED isolation level. MySQL defaults to REPEATABLE READ but this isn't verified or enforced in config. If developer changes isolation or deployment uses different config, locking could fail silently.
findings.fix: Add to Config class: 'SQLALCHEMY_ENGINE_OPTIONS = {"isolation_level": "READ COMMITTED", "pool_pre_ping": True, "pool_size": 10, "max_overflow": 20}'. Document in Section 2: application requires READ COMMITTED or REPEATABLE READ for row locking.

findings.title: Import Employee Validation Per-Row Commit Creates Partial Success State
findings.problem: Code commits after each row individually. If row 50 fails, rows 1-49 already committed. Users might expect all-or-nothing behavior but get partial success. Re-importing same file will update existing rows (not idempotent on failure).
findings.fix: Add implementation note documenting partial success by design: 'Import commits per-row. Failed rows don't rollback previous rows. Re-importing updates existing emp_ids.' Provide alternative all-or-nothing implementation if that behavior is required: collect all employees_to_add, then commit once at end.

findings.title: Undefined Behavior for Export with Zero Results
findings.problem: Design states 'Return empty Excel/CSV file with headers only' for zero results, but implementation 'df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=[...])' doesn't handle empty results correctly - pandas might not create columns properly if results is empty list.
findings.fix: Add check after query.all(): 'if not results: df = pd.DataFrame(columns=[...]) else: df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=[...])' to explicitly create empty DataFrame with headers when no results.

findings.title: Ambiguous Optional Manager ID Validation
findings.problem: Code uses 'manager_id = str(row.get("manager_id", "")).strip() or None' but doesn't handle common null representations in Excel/CSV like 'None', 'null', 'N/A', 'na', or pandas NaN. These become non-empty strings after str() conversion.
findings.fix: Use 'if pd.isna(manager_id_raw): manager_id = None' for pandas NaN. Then 'if manager_id.lower() in ["", "none", "null", "n/a", "na"]: manager_id = None' to handle common null representations.

findings.title: Date Filter Validation Missing Time Component Handling
findings.location: Section 6 (Export TAS Records) - date_from and date_to
findings.problem: Filters use 'datetime.fromisoformat(date_from)' for ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD' which creates 00:00:00 time. For date_to, '<= 2024-01-31 00:00:00' EXCLUDES all records from Jan 31 after midnight. Users expect date_to to include entire day.
findings.fix: For date_to: use 'date_to_end = datetime.fromisoformat(date_to) + timedelta(days=1)' then 'query.filter(TASRecord.submitted_at < date_to_end)' to include entire date_to. Or update docs to accept full datetime 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' format.
